- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap or slow the upward slope.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply a downward bias for days 1–5.
- Mean reversion is evident when model forecasts deviate >1.5σ from recent 7-day average; pull forecast toward historical mean.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment weight to forecast adjustment.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (>±20% from 14-day moving average) unless sentiment confirms breakout; cap or smooth outliers.
